candidates: Low-grade Chondrosarcoma of the Temporal Bone
key_facts: 2-year history of gradual-onset right facial weakness
No hearing loss, tinnitus, imbalance, or other cranial nerve deficits
Nonpulsatile mass in the inferior ear canal
Mild sensorineural hearing loss at 4000 Hz
Irregular lesion in the right mastoid near the stylomastoid foramen on MRI
Expansion of the fallopian canal and erosion of the posterior external auditory canal on CT
Specimen consisted of cartilage on gross examination
Pleomorphic hyperchromatic nuclei on microscopic examination
champion: Low-grade Chondrosarcoma of the Temporal Bone

raw.champion: Low-grade Chondrosarcoma of the Temporal Bone
raw.rationale: The presence of a cartilaginous specimen on gross examination and pleomorphic hyperchromatic nuclei on microscopic examination, along with the location of the lesion in the right mastoid near the stylomastoid foramen, are consistent with a diagnosis of Low-grade Chondrosarcoma of the Temporal Bone.

rejected.label: Facial Nerve Schwannoma
rejected.why: While the location near the stylomastoid foramen and the involvement of the facial nerve could suggest a schwannoma, the cartilaginous nature of the specimen and the specific microscopic findings are more indicative of a chondrosarcoma.
